In NIST CSF 2.0, the cybersecurity outcomes within the Core are arranged hierarchically by **Function, then Category, and finally Subcategory** [NIST.CSWP.29 p.7].

The six **Functions** organize cybersecurity outcomes at their highest level: GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER [NIST.CSWP.29 p.7].

Each Function is divided into **Categories**, which are related cybersecurity outcomes that collectively comprise the Function. **Subcategories** further divide each Category into more specific outcomes of technical and management activities [NIST.CSWP.29 p.10].

The order and size of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories does not imply their sequence or importance [NIST.CSWP.29 p.7].
